newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares fall on A share declines.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares fall on A share declines.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share index fell sharply in line with the domestic currency A share market, hurt by concerns that Beijing is mulling new anti-speculation measures, brokers said.
The B share index lost 4.08 points or 2.41 percent to 165.31 on thin turnover of HK$17.8 million.
The A index fell 11.76 points or 2.42 percent to 475.07 on turnover of 3.73 billion yuan.

"The performance of the B shares in the near future will continue to be tightly linked to the A share market, which has been hurt by investor jitters over a possible new crackdown by Beijing," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said in Shenzhen.
"Technical charts for the A shares look bad, indicating further falls," the analyst said, adding any further steep drops in the A index would weigh on B shares.
"The B share index is expected to consolidate between 160 to 170 points over the next few sessions," he said.
Investors largely stayed on the sidelines ahead of the scheduled Thursday listing of 100 million B shares of Nanjing Posts & Telecommunication Equipment Co Ltd in Shenzhen, analysts said.

"Nanjing Posts is likely to debut strongly given the company's bright earnings outlook and the solid performances put in by other recent company listings on their first day of trading," another analyst at a major Chinese brokerage said.
The listing of Nanjing Posts will give the B share market a boost on Thursday, analysts said.
On the B share market, conglomerate Gintian was the biggest loser, falling HK$0.34 or 9.83 percent to HK$3.12.
Shenzhen Energy was the worst A share performer, tumbling 1.44 yuan or 7.37 percent to 18.10 yuan.
The Shenzhen bourse on Monday said a probe had found illegal accounts opened for trading in Energy shares and it was conducting further investigations.
